Authorised Materials QC

 

Learn to compare the authorised materials, their conditions, quantities and restrictions, record the result and raise concerns with Senior Delivery.

About 90 minutes 12 sections 14 question self-test

No previous QC experience is needed. It assumes no prior knowledge of eAssessment, eVigilation or the eDash Materials lookup.

By the end you will be able to:

  • compare the platforms that apply to a unit, field by field
  • set the category and the outcome in the QC sheet
  • write a comment Senior Delivery can act on, and know when to raise something

Your first check is a real row in the sheet, and every unit receives an independent second QC by a Senior Delivery member.

Before your first check, ask your manager for access to the three platforms and the QC sheet.

Your progress is saved in this browser as you go, so you can stop and come back.

Authorised Materials QC · Process

Check that authorised materials agree across the relevant exam platforms and are clear enough for students and supervisors to follow.

Allow about 90 minutes 12 sections 16 worked examples 14 question self-test

Stage 1 of 4 Understand

01

Authorised materials: what they are and why we check them

How to use this guide

Read sections 1 to 12 in order the first time. They follow the order of an authorised materials check, and each step assumes the ones before it have been completed.

  1. Understand 01–02 Learn the purpose, your role and the platforms.
  2. Do 03–07 Prepare, open the platforms, choose the category, compare and record.
  3. Judge 08–11 Learn what happens next, look up terms, and practise with examples.
  4. Keep 12 Use the quick checklist when checking a real exam.

You do not need to memorise the guide. Use the glossary when a term is unfamiliar and keep the field guidance in section 6 beside you during a check. Once you understand the process, use the checklist in section 12 as a reminder of the steps, and search (⌘K) for anything else.

Authorised materials are the resources students are authorised to use during an exam, such as notes, calculators and working sheets. The authorised materials quality check (QC) compares the published list of authorised materials, the instructions and the exam rules before the exam runs, to check that they are consistent across the platforms and can be followed.

Students and supervisors use different platforms to read these instructions.

The authorised materials need to match across the platforms, so that students and supervisors have the same information and the same expectations.

QC identifies discrepancies or problems so they can be reviewed prior to the exam.

Your role

Who does what

In this guide, you are the staff member carrying out the first QC: the initial check of an exam’s authorised materials. An exam supervisor is the person supervising students during the exam. Senior Delivery staff are Matt Nixon and Kayla Sgambellone, who manage second QC and any required follow-up.

Every exam is checked twice. The first QC is yours. The second QC is an independent re-check of every applicable platform by Matt or Kayla, never by the person who did the first QC. Section 8 explains it.

Your responsibility is to compare the authorised materials and record your findings in a clear way.

ResponsibilityWho does it
Compare the information across the platforms.You
Record the category, outcome and any supporting comments needed.You
Record any rules or instructions supervisors may need to know about.You
Manage faculty clarification, corrections and supervisor reminders.Senior Delivery
1

You record, you do not resolve. If instructions conflict or need clarification, record the issue in your comments and tell Senior Delivery by Zoom or a Slack message. Raise it when you find it rather than waiting. They manage the decision or correction. Do not choose which platform should take priority, change exam content or contact the faculty yourself.

2

If the authorised materials or instructions are not clear, write down what is unclear. Note any difference between the platforms, any unclear instruction and anything unusual, in each platform’s own words. The sections that follow show you the platforms, the QC sheet where your notes go, and what to record. If you are unsure how to do something, ask Matt or Kayla rather than guessing.

02

The platforms you will use

The three platforms you compare, who reads each one, and which apply to each delivery period.

Each platform below records an exam’s authorised materials. Students read eAssessment, Online Supervisors read eVigilation, and the Delivery team uses the eDash Materials lookup for end of semester exams. You compare them because everyone involved needs instructions that mean the same thing. Their layouts differ: an item may appear in a named field on one platform and in free text on another.

Students use this

eAssessment

Check the exam page’s Instructions and Authorised Materials sections. Instructions is free text, so it carries conditions the other platforms have no field for.

Applies to every supervised exam
Online Supervisors use this

eVigilation

Check the Authorised Materials panel, opened from the information icon. Its fields are fixed, so wording that does not fit a field appears in free text, usually under Other.

Applies to every supervised exam
The Delivery team uses this

eDash Materials lookup

Check the exam’s card in eDash’s Delivery view, under Checks > Materials lookup. It lists every exam on the date you choose.

Applies to most end of semester exams: see the table below

Which platforms apply

The delivery period and the shell name together determine whether you compare two platforms or three. Establish it before opening the platforms, then make sure each one shows the same exam shell. An apparent materials mismatch may simply belong to a different sitting.

The delivery period is part of each exam’s shell name. For example, Sem 1 Deferred & Supplementary is a Deferred and Supplementary exam, not a Semester 1 main exam. Section 3 shows where to find the shell name in the QC sheet.

Stage 2 of 4 Do

03

Before you start a check

Learn what the QC sheet holds and the columns you fill in, then find a row that is ready to check and that nobody has done yet.

Where the work is recorded

Record your findings in the Authorised Materials QC 2026 sheet. The sheet lists the exams to check and holds the results of the checks. It is not one of the platforms you compare.

The QC sheet is your starting point. Each row represents one exam shell, a particular instance of an exam in eAssessment. A unit can have several shells for different groups or sittings, such as Australian, Malaysian and AAA (Alternative Assessment Arrangements) shells. Each shell is its own check, even when the shells share a unit code, and the shell name in Course Name col A tells you which one you have.

Getting access

Before your first session, check your access to eAssessment, eVigilation, the Delivery view in eDash and the QC sheet. If you do not have access, please see Matt or Kayla.

The columns you use

Columns A to F are populated automatically. You complete G, H and I; section 7 explains the entries.

ColNameUseWho fills it
ACourse NameIdentify the unit, period, sitting and cohort.Automatic
BLinkOpen the eAssessment shell.Automatic
DInvig TypeRead the supervision type. Unsupervised here confirms the exam is unsupervised, and its authorised materials are not checked.Automatic
EStart TimeSelect the exam date and check how soon it runs.Automatic
FEnrolment StatusThis is what decides readiness. Enrolled and Synced means the row is ready to check.Automatic
GAuth Mat CategorySelect the category that matches the authorised materials.You
HFirst QC OutcomeSelect the result of your comparison.You
ICommentsRecord findings, relevant authorised materials and supporting wording.You
J onwardsSenior Delivery columnsLeave the orange columns to Matt or Kayla.Senior Delivery

Find the rows to check

Rows are not allocated to you. Enrolment Status col F decides what to action: a row is ready for first QC once it reads Enrolled and Synced. Working by exam date helps you find the corresponding entry in each platform, since eVigilation and the Materials lookup both need a date set before they show anything.

  1. Open the Authorised Materials QC 2026 sheet. The Enrolled and Synced Shells tab lists the shells that are ready for a first QC.

  2. Filter Start Time col E to the nearest incomplete day.

  3. Confirm Enrolment Status col F reads Enrolled and Synced. That is the only test for readiness.

  4. If col G, col H or col I already contains information, this usually means it has been completed, so you do not need to redo it.

If the exam is within a week and the row reads Not Enrolled, raise it with Matt or Kayla.

If Invig Type col D reads Unsupervised, the authorised materials do not need to be checked. Select Unsupervised Exam in First QC Outcome col H, leave col G blank and write Unsupervised per Invig Type in Comments col I (Example 17).

How to complete a check

Work through one exam at a time.

  1. Find its row in the QC sheet and check that the exam is ready to review.

  2. Open the platforms required for its delivery period: eAssessment and eVigilation, plus the eDash Materials lookup where section 2 says it applies.

  3. Compare the authorised materials, rules and instructions. Check that the platforms match and that the instructions are clear enough to follow.

  4. Record the category, comparison outcome and supporting comments. Raise concerns with Senior Delivery for follow-up if required.

Stage 2 of 4 Do

04

Opening the applicable platforms

Choose the delivery period, then open each platform that applies in turn.

Section 2 sets out which platforms apply to each delivery period.

Choose the path for this delivery period

Select the delivery path before following the steps below, and the guide will show only the steps that apply to it.

Open eAssessment

  1. Open Link col B in the QC sheet.

  2. Check that the shell matches Course Name col A, including the period, sitting and cohort. Take particular care: a single unit can have an Australian and a Malaysian sitting, a main cohort and an AAA cohort, and a deferred shell.

  3. Read the category and every item under Authorised Materials.

  4. Read Instructions, including conditions on devices, software and copying.

  5. Compare the two sections. If they conflict, record both statements, continue the comparison and include all findings. Raise the conflict with Senior Delivery.

Open eVigilation

  1. Open Exam sessions.

  2. Set Select a date to the exam date in Start Time col E.

  3. Set Search by to Exam unit. Use Session to browse a whole date.

  4. Enter the unit code and search.

  5. Select the information icon on the row for the same shell, matching the sitting and cohort in Course Name col A.

  6. Read the category and all fields: Calculator, Dictionary, Notes, Other, Permitted Item, Textbook and Working Sheets. Read the wording beneath each indicator.

  7. Scroll to the bottom and check Hybrid and any answer sheet count.

Open the eDash Materials lookup for end of semester only

The eDash Materials lookup is the third platform for end of semester exams, except Malaysia-only shells and Suzhou (China) sittings. It is in eDash’s Delivery view, which only the Delivery team can open.

  1. Open eDash and select Open the Delivery view. The Delivery dashboard link also opens it directly.

  2. Select Materials lookup under Checks in the left sidebar.

  3. Set Exam date to the date in Start Time col E, then press Load materials. Nothing loads until you press it.

  4. Type the unit code in Find a unit code or quiz name and select the exam.

  5. Confirm the sitting matches Course Name col A. The same unit can appear more than once, for example an Australian and a Malaysian sitting, so use the quiz name and times to choose the right one.

  6. Read every field, including Other, and compare it with eAssessment and eVigilation. Values that mean nothing is permitted, such as None or N/A, show in grey, an empty cell shows as Blank, and a restriction such as Generative AI not authorised shows in red. eDash keeps a loaded date for 10 minutes, so press Reload if the details may have been corrected since you loaded it.

If a unit is missingCheck the exam date and Enrolment Status col F first. A missing eVigilation entry does not make an exam unsupervised: only Invig Type col D reading Unsupervised does. If the row is Enrolled and Synced but the platform remains unavailable or shows no authorised materials, explain what happened in Comments col I and tell Senior Delivery by Zoom or a Slack message. Follow Example 12 in section 11.

Stage 2 of 4 Do

05

Authorised materials categories

The six categories an exam can be, and how to choose the one you record.

The category describes the overall access to materials, such as Closed Book or Open Book. Individual conditions give the detail, including note limits and named software. Read both: a category heading alone does not tell you everything that is authorised or restricted. Choose the category from the materials the exam permits. If the authorised materials conflict with the stated category, record a Discrepancy. Open Access and Open Access with Additional Device are distinct categories, not interchangeable labels.

CategoryWhat it permitsCheck
Closed BookNo resources are permitted.Instructions do not permit items that conflict with the category.
Closed Book + SPISpecifically Permitted Items (SPI): a specified set of items, such as a calculator or limited notes.Each item and its conditions.
Open BookHardcopy reference materials, such as books, notes and dictionaries.Any permission for digital material.
Open Book with Additional DeviceOpen Book materials plus a laptop, tablet or monitor, not a phone.Device type, permitted use and internet conditions. Do not assume connectivity.
Open AccessBroad access to resources, subject to the exam’s restrictions.Gen AI and any other exclusions.
Open Access with Additional DeviceOpen Access plus a laptop, tablet or monitor, not a phone.Device type, permitted use and restrictions.

Category

Compare the category headings and the items each platform permits. Set col G from the authorised materials.

Record it this wayIf the category conflicts with the authorised materials listed, record a Discrepancy in col H and quote both in Comments col I.

Where the platforms conflict on the authorised materials themselves, still enter the exam’s most likely category in col G and describe the conflict in Comments. Do not leave col G blank while Senior Delivery resolves it. Ask Senior Delivery if the category is unclear.

Where each platform shows it

eAssessmentAnother unit, Authorised Materials
eVigilationBCH3021
eDash Materials lookupETF2480. The chip’s colour matches the QC sheet’s dropdown.

Each platform words the category its own way. Closed Book + SPI, for example, appears in eVigilation as Closed book with specifically permitted items and in the eDash Materials lookup as Specifically permitted items. In the Materials lookup, an option that is not one of the six standard options shows with a dashed outline and a warning to compare the wording with eAssessment and eVigilation. The eAssessment example is from a different unit.

06

Comparing what the platforms say

A field by field comparison of every platform that applies.

In this section
  • Compare fields
  • Record when unusual
Delivery period End of semester. Compare eAssessment, eVigilation and the eDash Materials lookup. All other deliveries. Compare eAssessment and eVigilation. The Materials lookup does not apply. Change

How to compare

Check one field at a time across every applicable platform so you can compare the whole entry before moving to the next item.

Ask two questions. Do the platforms allow the same materials under the same conditions? Could a student and supervisor understand and apply those conditions? Matching words do not settle the second question. If a permitted item or condition remains unclear, record the wording for Senior Delivery to review.

Compare these fields

Jump to a field
  • eA against itself
  • Calculator
  • Dictionary
  • Notes
  • Textbook
  • Working sheets
  • Other / Permitted
  • Additional device
  • Generative AI
  • Answer sheets, Hybrid
  • Copying, translation

Decide if the wording conflicts

FindingWhat to do
Categories, authorised materials, restrictions or quantities conflict, within a platform or between platforms.Record a Discrepancy, quote the conflict and continue checking the remaining fields. For example, eA permits 5 working sheets and the Materials lookup says 99, meaning unlimited (Example 3).
Different words describe the same item.Do not treat wording differences as a discrepancy. Record the comparison where relevant. For example, eVig says Notes - Double sided A4 x 1 - Physical Only and eA says one double sided A4 page of physical notes (Example 5).
The same item is recorded in a different field, such as under Other rather than its named field. Other is where eVigilation and the Materials lookup put anything that does not fit a named field, often because the named field has a length limit.Not a discrepancy. Select Other in First QC Outcome col H and say in Comments which field the item is sitting in. For example, eVig Notes reads None but Other permits the same notes (Example 4).
Only one platform has a place to state something, and the others say nothing about it.Silence alone is not a discrepancy. Check Other and Permitted Item for anything opposing, then record what that platform says if it departs from the norm. For example, a copy and paste restriction appears only in eAssessment Instructions (Example 9).
The platforms agree, but the instruction is unclear, contradictory or unusual enough to need review.Record All Match but Escalation Required, explain the concern and raise it with Senior Delivery. For example, a mobile phone permission (Example 16), or pens and pencils with no paper described (Example 15).

Select a field to see how to compare it and where each platform shows it. Most strips show one exam, ETF2480, on every platform, so you can see how each one records the same materials. A strip that uses other units says so.

eAssessment against itself

Compare Instructions with Authorised Materials. Record any conflict, quoting both statements.

Keep goingContinue comparing the remaining fields and record all findings. Raise the conflict with Senior Delivery; do not decide which statement takes priority.

Calculator

Check the Calculator field, Instructions and Other. Compare physical or virtual calculators, named products and model restrictions. Record the type when the platforms differ or the wording is unclear, such as “faculty approved calculator”.

A physical calculator and Excel listed under Other are two separate authorised items. Do not assume other calculator software is allowed.

Notes

Compare the permitted format and any stated limits: size, quantity, single or double sided, physical or digital, and handwritten or printed. Record the wording where the meaning differs between platforms, or a limit is unclear. Different wording with the same meaning needs no comment.

Different wording can describe the same item. If all platforms permit “one folder of printed notes” without a page count, record the wording in Comments; this alone does not require escalation.

Record it this wayIf a Notes field says None but Other permits the same notes the other platforms state, that is the same item in a different field, not a disagreement. Select Other in col H and say in Comments which field it is sitting in.

Working sheets

Read the Working Sheets field and any quantity in Instructions. Record each platform’s wording or number where they differ.

ValueMeaning
YesWorking sheets are permitted. This value alone gives no quantity.
A specified count, such as 5 or FiveThat number of working sheets.
99 in the Materials lookupUnlimited working sheets.
UnlimitedNo quantity limit.
No, None, 0, Zero, N/A or NANo working sheets.

5 against Yes is not a discrepancy on that difference alone, because Yes can accompany a limited or unlimited number. 5 against 99 is a discrepancy, because five differs from unlimited. Compare any additional restrictions in the platforms.

Other and Permitted Item

Other is where eVigilation and the Materials lookup put anything that does not fit a named field. Read eVigilation’s Other and Permitted Item fields, the Materials lookup’s Other field and eAssessment Instructions in full. Look for software, formula sheets, unusual items and restrictions. Compare their meaning with the rest of the page and the other platforms. Record relevant wording.

Record it this wayA formula sheet mentioned or provided but absent from the authorised materials list is a Discrepancy. This applies whether it is embedded in the exam, separately linked or a hard copy the student brings to the exam sitting. Record its type, page count and how it is accessed.

Additional device

Check the device permission in Instructions: device type, allowed use, internet access and limits on communication, Gen AI or applications. Check other platforms’ free-text fields for opposing conditions. Record the exact wording and raise missing or conflicting conditions.

Escalate this onePermission to use a mobile phone during the assessment requires escalation to Senior Delivery, even if the platforms agree. Routine instructions to photograph or upload hybrid answers after the exam do not require escalation on that basis alone.

eVigilation

No device field. Look for device conditions under Other.

Generative AI

The platforms always state that Gen AI is not authorised, unless the Chief Examiner has allowed it. That is the norm, so you do not need to record it. Check whether any platform permits Gen AI, including any limits on its use. If one does, compare the others and record the wording, starting with Gen AI permitted so the comment is clear.

Permission to use a named application does not necessarily permit its AI functions. Record unclear limits rather than deciding them yourself.

When the platforms differIf one platform permits Gen AI and another says it is not authorised, that is a Discrepancy. Quote both. If one permits it and another says nothing about Gen AI, that is not a discrepancy: select All Match and record Gen AI permitted.

Where each platform shows it

eAssessmentInstructions, as it reads on every exam where Gen AI is not authorised
eVigilation

No Gen AI field. Look for it under Other.

eDash Materials lookupETF2480. The Materials lookup has its own Generative AI status field.

Answer sheets and Hybrid

Check Hybrid at the bottom of eVigilation and read the answer sheet instructions in eAssessment. Compare any stated answer sheet quantities. Record conflicting counts, or a paper component with no clear answer sheet instructions.

When you record answer sheets, give the Hybrid flag and each platform’s count separately. Hybrid yes or no is not a quantity. Note: answer sheets are not working sheets.

Escalate this oneIf all platforms permit pens and pencils but describe no working or answer sheets, and Hybrid is No, record the contradiction in Comments and escalate to Senior Delivery. Use All Match but Escalation Required for that case.

Where each platform shows it

eAssessmentETF2480, Authorised Materials: the answer sheet count. There is no Hybrid flag.Instructions: how students upload paper answers
eVigilationETF2480
eDash Materials lookupETF2480

Copying and translation restrictions

Every eExam carries the standard eExam Terms and Conditions, which say students may not copy or paste text to or from external sources unless their Chief Examiner has authorised it. That is the norm, so you do not record it.

Some exams add their own rules in eAssessment Instructions, such as a Rules for Copy/paste to OR from external sources section. Those are not standard, so record them. eVigilation and the Materials lookup have no field for copy and paste, so record the rules as eAssessment states them. Their silence is not disagreement.

Use COPY AND PASTE RESTRICTIONS as a comment label, followed by the actual rule. Translation is different: another platform can state a translation permission in a free-text field, so compare it and record any opposing statement. A ban on browser extensions can coexist with permission for a separate translation website.

Which copy and paste rules to record

Standard: do not recordeExam Terms and Conditions, in every exam
Not standard: record itThe exam’s own Instructions

Record these items when they are unusual

These conditions often appear on only one platform, so an All Match outcome does not show them. Each one has a norm that applies to every exam: the eExam Terms and Conditions rule out anything that has not been authorised, Gen AI is not authorised, and copying or pasting to or from external sources is not allowed. Record an item in Comments col I only when the exam departs from that norm, even if the platforms agree. Calculator, notes and working sheets appear on every platform, so you compare them, and record them only when the platforms differ in meaning or the wording is unclear.

ItemRecord it when
Gen AIA platform permits it. Record Gen AI permitted and any conditions.
Copy and pasteThe exam’s Instructions add their own rules beyond the standard Terms and Conditions. Record the rules as written.
TranslationA translation tool, website or condition is stated. Record what it allows and any limits.
SoftwareSoftware is permitted. Record the names, packages and, where stated, where they may run.
Formula sheetsA formula sheet is provided or permitted. Record its type, page count and how students receive or access it.
Local files and MoodleAccess is permitted. Record the named files or the scope of access.
Additional deviceA device is permitted. Record its type, permitted use and restrictions.
Unfamiliar itemsYou have not seen the item before. Record what is permitted and where it is noted.

Stage 2 of 4 Do

07

Recording the result

Three cells belong to you: what each one is for, how they differ, and the conditions supervisors need to know about.

Three different things

The three entries answer different questions. Category describes the exam’s authorised materials, outcome describes your comparison, and comments explain the finding. The same category can have a matching result or a discrepancy; choosing a category does not establish that the platforms agree.

A matching exam can still need comments and a supervisor reminder. Senior Delivery decides on reminders separately from the QC outcome.

  1. Set Auth Mat Category col G to the category the exam actually is.

  2. Set First QC Outcome col H, using the table below.

  3. Write what you found in Comments col I: anything other than a clean match, plus anything from the Record when unusual list that departs from the norm, even when every platform agrees. Name each platform and quote its wording.

Choose the first QC outcome

Choose the outcome from the check as a whole. One conflicting category, item or quantity is enough for Discrepancy even if the remaining fields agree. When platforms agree but an unclear, contradictory or unusual instruction needs review, use All Match but Escalation Required and explain why. If you could not complete the comparison, follow When you need help below.

OutcomeUse it when
All Match (eVig, eA, Lookup)All applicable platforms agree, the instructions can be followed and no concern requires escalation. Record anything unusual from the list in section 6. See Examples 2, 5 and 9.
DiscrepancyCategories, authorised materials, restrictions or quantities conflict within or between platforms, or a formula sheet is missing from the authorised materials list. Quote the finding and tell Senior Delivery. See Examples 1, 3 and 10.
All Match but Escalation RequiredPlatforms agree, but an unclear, contradictory or unusual instruction needs review. Explain the concern and raise it with Senior Delivery. See Examples 15 and 16.
OtherThe check finds a deviation from the norm, or something that needs to be noted, that no other outcome covers, such as the same item recorded in a different field (Example 4). Explain it in Comments. Unusual items that every platform agrees on, such as Gen AI permitted, stay All Match with a comment.
Unsupervised ExamThe assessment has no supervision: Invig Type col D reads Unsupervised. Leave col G blank, write Unsupervised per Invig Type in Comments and do not check the authorised materials. See Example 17.

The value name lists three platformsUse All Match (eVig, eA, Lookup) for a matching two-platform check too. The dropdown label does not change which platforms apply. Lookup in the label now means the eDash Materials lookup.

When you need help

SituationWhat to do
Unclear published wordingQuote it in Comments. Use Discrepancy if the platforms conflict, or All Match but Escalation Required if they agree but need clarification.
A required platform will not open or shows no authorised materials, or an Enrolled and Synced unit remains missingExplain what happened in Comments col I, then tell Senior Delivery by Zoom or a Slack message. Do not choose a category or outcome from an incomplete comparison.
A procedure or field is unfamiliarAsk Matt or Kayla before recording the result.
An exam that looks unsupervisedCheck Invig Type col D. Select Unsupervised Exam only if it reads Unsupervised; its authorised materials then do not need checking. A missing eVigilation entry is not enough.
A row marked Not EnrolledIt is not ready to check. Skip it and leave G, H and I blank, as in section 3.

Write a useful comment

Write enough for another checker to find the issue without asking what you meant. Name each platform, quote only the relevant wording and say what needs attention. Write generative AI as Gen AI. A comment such as “notes do not match” is too vague.

Too vagueWrite this instead
Notes do not matchNotes: eA permits “one double sided A4 page of physical notes”. eVig permits the same page, recorded under Other, with the Notes field reading “None”. Same notes, different field.
Calculator does not matchCalculator: eA and eVig specify a physical calculator. eDash says “faculty approved calculator”; the permitted type needs clarification.
Platforms disagree on translationTranslation: eA permits an online translation website for single words. eVig Other says “No translation tools permitted”.

Escalations and supervisor reminders

Escalation means referring an issue to Senior Delivery for a decision or clarification: you record it in Comments col I and tell them by Zoom or a Slack message, and they decide what happens next. A supervisor reminder draws attention to a condition that needs to be noticed during the exam, and clear, matching authorised materials can still need one. Senior Delivery decides which units receive a reminder. Your part is to record the conditions a reminder is based on, using the Record when unusual list in section 6, and anything else a supervisor would need to know in advance.

Senior Delivery works from the QC Overview tab, which is built from your Comments. Describe each condition clearly so the reminder reaches the right unit.

Previous6. Comparing what the platforms sayNext8. Second QC

Stage 3 of 4 Judge

08

Second QC

What happens after your first QC, and what to raise before the exam.

The second QC

Every unit, including those you recorded as a clean match, receives a second QC by a Senior Delivery member who did not do the first check. It is a full re-check of the authorised materials, instructions and exam rules on every applicable platform, not a review of your comment, and the result goes in col J. Your comments support that check; they do not replace it.

Follow up before the exam

Raise any discrepancy, escalation or platform you could not check as soon as you find it: record it in Comments col I, then tell Matt or Kayla by Zoom or a Slack message. The week before the exam is a backstop, not a waiting period. Raise these with Matt or Kayla when the exam is within a week:

1

The unit still has no first QC outcome.

2

A discrepancy or escalation remains unresolved. A faculty needs time to answer.

3

The unit is still marked Not Enrolled.

Start early enough to allow the second QC and any faculty response. A first QC completed the day before an exam leaves no time for either.

Check for new rows

After finishing an exam date, check for units added since you filtered. Use the Enrolled and Synced Shells and QC Overview tabs to find outstanding work, then continue to the next exam date.

Stage 3 of 4 Judge

09

Glossary

The terms used throughout this process, to look up whenever one is unfamiliar.

The glossary is alphabetical. Each term is also explained where it first matters, so you do not need to memorise this page. The ones you will meet most often are exam shell, Enrolled and Synced, discrepancy and Senior Delivery.

TermDefinition
AAAAlternative Assessment Arrangements: adjustments for individual students, such as extra time or specialised equipment. Students with AAA can be in a separate exam shell, which is checked on its own row.
Authorised materialsThe list of materials students are authorised to use during their eExam, and the terms on which they may use them: how many of each item, and the conditions and restrictions attached. All of this information is compared, not the items alone. See section 6.
Chief ExaminerThe academic responsible for a unit’s exam. Only the Chief Examiner can authorise what the standard rules do not allow, such as Gen AI or copying and pasting from external sources.
CohortA group of students within a unit who sit the same exam shell, such as the main cohort or an AAA cohort.
Deferred and SupplementaryA later sitting of an exam, for students granted a deferred exam or offered a supplementary one. Section 2 lists the platforms it uses.
Delivery periodWhen an exam runs, such as the Semester 1 or Semester 2 main exam period, in-semester or Deferred and Supplementary. It is part of the shell name in Course Name col A and, with the rest of the shell name, decides which platforms you compare. See section 2.
DiscrepancyA conflict in categories, authorised materials, restrictions or quantities, within a platform or between platforms. A formula sheet that is mentioned or provided but missing from the authorised materials list is also a discrepancy. The same item recorded in a different field is not.
eAThe eAssessment platform. This abbreviation appears in comments and outcome labels.
eDashMonash’s exam-day dashboard. Its Delivery view, which only the Delivery team can open, has the Materials lookup. This name appears in comments.
eDash Materials lookupThe screen in eDash’s Delivery view that shows each exam’s authorised materials by date. The third platform for end of semester exams only. See section 4.
End of semesterThe Semester 1 and Semester 2 main exam periods. Section 2 lists which of these exams also use the eDash Materials lookup.
Enrolled and SyncedThe status showing that the shell is ready to check. See section 3.
EscalationReferring an issue to Senior Delivery for a decision or clarification. See section 7.
eVigThe eVigilation platform. This abbreviation appears in comments and outcome labels.
Exam shellOne instance of an exam in eAssessment. Each shell needs its own check.
Gen AIGenerative artificial intelligence. It is not authorised unless the Chief Examiner allows it, so record it only when an exam permits it.
HybridAn exam with a paper answer component: at least one question in the eExam requires a handwritten response. Check the answer sheet instructions separately from working sheets.
In-semester assessmentAn assessment during teaching, outside the main exam periods. Compare eAssessment and eVigilation.
In-Venue SupervisorSupervises students in an exam venue, using eDash on a tablet. See section 2.
Invig TypeThe supervision type in col D, such as Supervised-RI-RecordOnly or Unsupervised. Ask Senior Delivery if a code is unfamiliar.
LookupThe third platform in the outcome value All Match (eVig, eA, Lookup). For end of semester QC this is now the eDash Materials lookup. In comments, write eDash.
Lookup ToolThe Authorised Materials Search. It has been replaced as a QC platform by the eDash Materials lookup.
Not EnrolledThe exam shell is not ready to check. See section 3.
Online SupervisorSupervises students online and reads eVigilation. See section 2.
QC sheetThe Authorised Materials QC 2026 Google Sheet. It lists the exams to check and holds your results. See section 3.
Senior DeliveryMatt Nixon and Kayla Sgambellone. They manage the orange columns, second QC and escalation.
SittingOne delivery of an exam for a particular location or time.
SPISpecifically Permitted Items: specific resources students can refer to in a Closed Book eExam, as in Closed Book + SPI.
Supervisor reminderA note that draws a supervisor’s attention to a condition during the exam. Senior Delivery decides on reminders; you record the conditions they are based on. See section 7.
Unsupervised examAn assessment with no supervision, shown by Unsupervised in Invig Type col D. Its authorised materials are not checked. See section 7.
Working sheetsBlank sheets for working out during an exam. These are separate from hybrid answer sheets.

Stage 3 of 4 Judge

10

One check, worked through

A single check from the row in the sheet to the three cells filled in. Read it before the self-test.

This example connects the steps you have just learned, from choosing the correct platforms to writing the three entries. Notice how each entry follows from the comparison, and why Comments may still contain detail when the outcome is All Match.

A teaching example, not a real rowIt is illustrative, not a real unit or a scored question. The rules applied to it are the ones set out in sections 2 to 8. Work through it by reading, then use section 11 to test the decisions.

  1. Check the row. The shell is ACC2100 2026 Sem 1 Deferred & Supplementary. Invig Type col D shows a supervised type, Enrolment Status col F reads Enrolled and Synced, and col G, col H and col I are empty.

  2. Choose the platforms. Deferred and Supplementary uses eAssessment and eVigilation.

  3. Read eAssessment. The category is Closed Book + SPI. Both Authorised Materials and Instructions permit a physical calculator and one double sided A4 page of physical notes. Working sheets: None. Instructions also prohibit copying between the notes and response box. No paper answer component is described.

  4. Read eVigilation. The category and physical calculator match. Notes reads Notes - Double sided A4 x 1 - Physical Only. Working Sheets reads None. Dictionary, Textbook, Other and Permitted Item contain nothing further. Hybrid reads No.

  5. Compare. The notes wording means the same thing. The working sheet quantities match. All other applicable fields agree, and the stated authorised materials are clear. The copying restriction sits in eAssessment Instructions, where it belongs.

  6. Record the result as shown below.

What goes in the three cells

Nothing here disagrees, so the only thing worth recording is the copying restriction. It is stated in eAssessment, which is the only platform with a place for it.

col GClosed Book + SPI col HAll Match (eVig, eA, Lookup) col ICOPY AND PASTE RESTRICTIONS: eA Instructions prohibit copying between the notes and response box.

What happens nextSenior Delivery carries out the second QC and decides whether the copying restriction needs a reminder. Neither is yours to complete.

11

Worked examples and self-test

Seventeen cases, fourteen of them scored.

0 of 14 answered

There are 17 cases and 14 scored questions. Examples 6, 8 and 17 are reference cases. The pass mark is 12 out of 14, using first-attempt answers.

For each case, identify the authorised materials and restrictions, compare the platforms and decide what needs recording. Use the earlier sections when needed; the questions practise applying the process.

Use Test yourself to answer before revealing the explanation. Reference shows the worked answers. Where a case says All Match, assume the other applicable fields agree, can be followed and raise no separate concern requiring escalation.

DiscrepancyAn additional device▸
What you see
The eAssessment heading reads Open Access. Instructions permit a laptop or tablet, not a phone, with internet access. eVigilation has no device instruction; the other details agree.
What to do
Select Open Access with Additional Device in col G. Open Access is a different category, so record the conflict as Discrepancy in col H. Include the device permission and both categories in Comments.
What to enter
col GOpen Access with Additional Devicecol HDiscrepancycol IeA permits an internet-connected laptop or tablet, not a phone. This fits Open Access with Additional Device, but the eA heading reads Open Access. eVig has no device instruction.

Based on the authorised materials stated, which value belongs in Auth Mat Category, col G?

All MatchGenerative AI permission▸
What you see
eAssessment, eVigilation and the eDash Materials lookup explicitly permit Gen AI. The permission is clear and consistent, with no conflicting instruction.
What to do
Select All Match and record the permission. Senior Delivery decides whether a reminder is needed. A clear permission does not need faculty clarification merely because it concerns Gen AI.
What to enter
col GThe category supported by the authorised materialscol HAll Match (eVig, eA, Lookup)col IGen AI permitted in eA Instructions, eVig and eDash. All three agree.

All platforms agree. What belongs in First QC Outcome, col H?

DiscrepancyWorking sheet quantities▸
What you see
eAssessment permits 5 working sheets. eVigilation says Yes. The eDash Materials lookup says 99.
What to do
Yes confirms permission without a quantity. 99 means unlimited. The discrepancy is between eAssessment’s five-sheet limit and the Materials lookup’s unlimited permission.
What to enter
col GThe category supported by the authorised materialscol HDiscrepancycol IWorking sheets: eA permits 5; eVig says Yes, with no quantity; eDash says 99, meaning unlimited. eA and eDash quantities conflict.

What belongs in First QC Outcome, col H?

OtherNotes recorded in the wrong field▸
What you see
eAssessment permits “one double sided A4 page of physical notes”. eVigilation Notes reads None, and Other permits the same page of notes.
What to do
The platforms permit the same thing, so this is not a discrepancy. eVigilation fields have length limits, so an item is sometimes recorded under Other instead. Select Other in col H and say in Comments which field the item is sitting in.
What to enter
col GThe category supported by the authorised materialscol HOthercol INotes: eA and eVig both permit “one double sided A4 page of physical notes”. In eVig it is recorded under Other and the Notes field reads “None”. Same notes, different field.

Both platforms permit the same page of notes, but eVig records it under Other. What belongs in First QC Outcome, col H?

All MatchDifferent words with the same meaning▸
What you see
eVigilation says Notes - Double sided A4 x 1 - Physical Only. eAssessment says “One double sided A4 page of physical notes is permitted.”
What to do
Both describe the same size, quantity and format. Select All Match. Nothing here needs recording: the wording differs but the authorised materials are identical and both platforms state it.
What to enter
col GThe category supported by the authorised materialscol HAll Match (eVig, eA, Lookup)col INo entry needed. The notes wording differs between eVig and eA but states the same notes.

What belongs in First QC Outcome, col H?

Escalation RequiredUndefined notes permission▸
What you see
The applicable platforms agree that “open notes” are permitted. Neither the exam page nor the unit’s other published information defines the phrase.
What to do
Record the wording and request clarification through Senior Delivery. Do not borrow a definition from another unit. If this unit publishes a clear definition that resolves the uncertainty, record it and reassess the outcome.
What to enter
col GThe category supported by the authorised materialscol HAll Match but Escalation Requiredcol IAll platforms permit “open notes”, but no definition was found in the unit’s published information. The permitted format and limits need clarification.
All MatchA physical calculator and Excel▸
What you see
eAssessment Instructions permit a physical calculator and Excel. eVigilation lists the calculator under Calculator and Excel under Other.
What to do
The authorised materials match. Record Excel, because permitted software is one of the unusual items in section 6; the calculator matches and needs no comment. Excel sitting under Other does not create a discrepancy or permit other unnamed software.
What to enter
col GClosed Book + SPIcol HAll Match (eVig, eA, Lookup)col ISoftware: Excel permitted in eA Instructions and under eVig Other.

What belongs in First QC Outcome, col H?

DiscrepancyA formula sheet▸
What you see
The exam mentions or provides a formula sheet that is absent from the authorised materials list.
What to do
Record Discrepancy whether the sheet is embedded in the exam, separately linked or a hard copy the student brings to the exam sitting. Record its type, page count, how students access it and the missing list entry.
What to enter
col GThe category supported by the authorised materialscol HDiscrepancycol IFormula sheet: [type and pages], accessed [where or how]. Not listed under authorised materials. Exam wording: “[quote]”.
All MatchCopy and paste restrictions▸
What you see
eAssessment Instructions add a rule against copying between the notes and response box. This goes beyond the standard eExam Terms and Conditions. eVigilation and the Materials lookup have no field for copy and paste restrictions.
What to do
Silence alone is not a discrepancy. Record the restriction, because it is not the standard rule. Senior Delivery decides whether a supervisor reminder is needed.
What to enter
col GThe category supported by the authorised materialscol HAll Match (eVig, eA, Lookup)col ICOPY AND PASTE RESTRICTIONS: eA Instructions prohibit copying between the notes and response box.

No other platform has a field for this restriction. Is their silence a Discrepancy?

DiscrepancyOpposing translation permissions▸
What you see
eAssessment permits an online translation website for single words. eVigilation Other says “No translation tools permitted”.
What to do
These are opposing permissions. Record Discrepancy and quote both. This differs from banning browser translation extensions while allowing a separate website, which can be consistent.
What to enter
col GThe category supported by the authorised materialscol HDiscrepancycol IeA permits an online translation website for single words. eVig Other: “No translation tools permitted”.

What belongs in First QC Outcome, col H?

All MatchSeparate shells for one unit▸
What you see
You are checking the main cohort shell in col A. Its platforms agree. The unit also has an AAA shell on a separate row and date.
What to do
Check this row independently. Another shell for the same unit does not create a discrepancy or share this outcome.
What to enter
col GThe category supported by the authorised materialscol HAll Match (eVig, eA, Lookup)col INo entry needed, unless something from the section 6 list is unusual.

Does the AAA shell existing make this row a Discrepancy?

Investigate firstA unit missing from eVigilation▸
What you see
A unit in the QC sheet cannot be found in eVigilation. Invig Type col D shows a supervised type. You have not checked the possible causes.
What to do
First confirm the exam date filter. Next check Enrolment Status col F. For an unchecked Not Enrolled row, skip and leave G, H and I blank; raise it with Matt or Kayla if the exam is within a week. If an Enrolled and Synced unit remains missing, explain the issue in Comments and tell Senior Delivery by Zoom or a Slack message.
Recording
Had col D read Unsupervised, you would set col H to Unsupervised Exam instead. For an Enrolled and Synced unit whose absence remains unexplained, write in col I which platform and unit could not be found, note that the date was checked, and inform Senior Delivery. Do not guess an outcome or treat the unit as unsupervised.

What do you do first?

All MatchSoftware running locally▸
What you see
All applicable platforms permit the same named software, such as Mathematica, R or Visual Studio, running from the student’s local drive.
What to do
Record the software and where it runs: on the student’s machine rather than a browser or cloud service. Permitted software is one of the unusual items in section 6. Senior Delivery decides on reminders under section 7.
What to enter
col GThe category supported by the authorised materialscol HAll Match (eVig, eA, Lookup)col ISoftware: [names], permitted to run locally on the student’s machine. All applicable platforms agree.

The platforms agree. What is your responsibility for this unit?

All MatchA folder of notes▸
What you see
All applicable platforms permit “one folder of printed notes” with no page count. There is no conflicting instruction.
What to do
Select All Match and record the wording in Comments. The absence of a page count does not by itself require escalation.
What to enter
col GThe category supported by the authorised materialscol HAll Match (eVig, eA, Lookup)col INotes: “one folder of printed notes”, with no page count. Same wording in all applicable platforms.

The platforms agree. What belongs in First QC Outcome, col H?

Escalation RequiredWriting equipment without paper instructions▸
What you see
All three platforms permit pens and pencils. None describes working sheets or answer sheets, and Hybrid reads No.
What to do
Record the contradiction in Comments and escalate to Senior Delivery. Select All Match but Escalation Required: the platforms agree, but the writing permission lacks paper instructions.
What to enter
col GThe category supported by the authorised materialscol HAll Match but Escalation Requiredcol IPens and pencils permitted. No working or answer sheets described in any applicable platform; Hybrid No. Please clarify what students may write on.

All applicable platforms agree and paper provision has been checked. What belongs in col H?

Escalation RequiredA mobile phone permission▸
What you see
All applicable platforms permit using a mobile phone during the assessment, beyond photographing or uploading hybrid answers afterwards.
What to do
Record the unusual permission and escalate to Senior Delivery. Select All Match but Escalation Required, even though the platforms agree. Routine hybrid instructions to photograph or upload answers after the exam do not require escalation on that basis alone.
What to enter
col GThe category supported by the authorised materialscol HAll Match but Escalation Requiredcol IAll applicable platforms permit mobile phone use during the assessment, beyond the normal hybrid answer-upload process. Unusual permission raised with Senior Delivery for review.

The platforms agree on this phone permission. What belongs in First QC Outcome, col H?

Unsupervised ExamAn unsupervised exam▸
What you see
Invig Type col D reads Unsupervised. The exam does not appear in eVigilation.
What to do
Select Unsupervised Exam. The authorised materials of an unsupervised exam do not need to be checked, so you do not compare the platforms. Col D is the confirmation: a missing eVigilation entry on its own is not (Example 12).
What to enter
col GLeave blankcol HUnsupervised Examcol IUnsupervised per Invig Type
